STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3, u4, u5

TRANSITION_FUNCTION:

(u0, has_door_key & !blocker_moved, u2) -> 0.1
(u1, has_door_key, u3) -> 0.1

feedback: Accepted. Header check: STATES declares u0-u5, INITIAL_STATE is u0, and FINAL_STATES (u5) is nonempty, declared, and accepting for the task (entered only on target_picked_up). Semantic fidelity: u0 (nothing done) -> u1 (ball moved) / u2 (key held) captures the required 'either order', u3 (both milestones), u4 (door unlocked/open), u5 (box carried) matches the task exactly. Soundness: reaching u5 requires blocker_moved, has_door_key, door_open, and target_picked_up to have fired, and else self-loops never advance, so there is no shortcut; the environment's own constraints (door cannot open while the ball blocks the only toggle cell or without the key; box unreachable before door_open) are mirrored by the u3->u4 and u4->u5 guards. Ordered transition coverage: u0's two guards (blocker_moved vs has_door_key & !blocker_moved) are mutually exclusive so first-match evaluation is deterministic; every state ends in an else self-loop. Predicate/event distinction: key_lost is a one-step event irrelevant to this task and is correctly absorbed by the per-state else loops in u1, u2, u3, and u4 (e.g., the mandatory key drop before picking up the ball or box cannot stall or misroute the machine); no transition keys on it. Regressions: blocker_moved, has_door_key, and door_open can all revert, but milestone latching is correct here - u1->u3 firing while the ball sits re-blocked is harmless because u3->u4 still requires door_open, which cannot occur until the ball is moved again, and no transition can be re-fired (u0, u1, u2, u3, u4 exits are one-way), preventing reward farming from re-picking the ball, re-picking the key, or re-toggling the door. Reward safety: rewards are nonnegative, dense on every progress transition (0.1 x4, 0.2, 1.0), bounded at 1.4 total, and the REWARD_FUNCTION guards exactly mirror the six progress transitions with else loops implicitly 0. Reachability/compactness: all six states are reachable via both orders; six states is appropriately compact for a four-milestone task with order tracking, using only the five supplied propositions (no invented predicates). Trace replay of the seed-0 example (pickup ball, drop, pickup key, toggle, drop key, pickup box) advances u0->u1->u3->u4->u5 with the expected rewards, including the key drop at step 19 being correctly absorbed by the u4 else loop.

All five environment-declared propositions are implemented and no extra functions, imports, actions, or side effects are present. blocker_moved: scans every cell for a door with a ball at (x-1, y); since the environment has exactly one door and the ball starts at (door.x-1, door.y), this is equivalent to the documented check of that single cell. It is a correct persistent reading: false initially (ball on the cell), true after pickup (ball in hand is not on the grid), and false again if the ball is dropped back onto that cell. The x=0 boundary call env.grid.get(-1, y) is safe because Grid.get returns None for out-of-bounds coordinates and the code guards with 'is not None'. has_door_key, door_open, and target_picked_up match the documented expressions exactly: carried key whose color matches a door present on the grid, any open door on the grid, and carrying a box whose color matches the env.mission string. key_lost implements the documented event prev['has_door_key'] and not K and not D, comparing the read-only previous_valuation snapshot against current state; the truthiness guard on the snapshot is harmless (it is a nonempty complete valuation each step) and nothing mutates the environment or episode memory. Event semantics are correct (true for exactly one step after the drop, not lingering), and the pairwise constraints hold by construction: key_lost excludes has_door_key and door_open (explicit 'not' terms) and cannot coincide with target_picked_up (the drop leaves hands empty, so the pickup happens at least one step later when prev['has_door_key'] is false). The example trace is reproduced correctly, including key_lost staying false at the step-19 drop because the door is open. All returns are boolean, syntax is valid, and only documented API surface (env.grid.get, env.carrying, env.mission, env.width, env.height, env.episode_memory['previous_valuation'], object type/color/is_open) is used.
